cases.setup_script:
set -e
/usr/bin/python3 - "$HOME" <<'PYK'
import sys
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric.ed25519 import Ed25519PrivateKey
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives import serialization as s
k = Ed25519PrivateKey.from_private_bytes(bytes(range(1, 33)))
open(sys.argv[1] + '/key', 'wb').write(k.private_bytes(s.Encoding.PEM, s.PrivateFormat.OpenSSH, s.NoEncryption()))
open(sys.argv[1] + '/key.pub', 'wb').write(k.public_key().public_bytes(s.Encoding.OpenSSH, s.PublicFormat.OpenSSH) + b' fixture-signer\n')
PYK
chmod 600 "$HOME/key"
/usr/bin/ssh-keygen -q -t ed25519 -N '' -C fixture-other -f "$HOME/other"
read -r kt kk kc < "$HOME/key.pub"
printf 'fixture@example.com namespaces="git" %s %s\n' "$kt" "$kk" > "$HOME/allowed_signers"
cat > ed-g <<'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
{ printf 'msg-G\n'; /bin/cat "$1"; } > "$1.new" && /bin/mv "$1.new" "$1"
EOF
sed 's/msg-G/msg-C/' ed-g > ed-c; sed 's/msg-G/msg-V/' ed-g > ed-v; sed 's/msg-G/msg-E/' ed-g > ed-e
printf '#!/bin/sh\nexit 3\n' > ed-fail
cat > fakegpg <<'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
/bin/cat > /dev/null
printf -- '-----BEGIN PGP SIGNATURE-----\n\nZml4dHVyZQ==\n-----END PGP SIGNATURE-----\n'
printf '[GNUPG:] SIG_CREATED D 1 8 00 1 FIXTUREFPR\n' >&2
EOF
cat > seq-edit <<'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
# todo: pick c2,c3,c4 -> pick c3, pick c2, drop c4
set -- "$1"
l2=$(/usr/bin/grep ' c2$' "$1"); l3=$(/usr/bin/grep ' c3$' "$1"); l4=$(/usr/bin/grep ' c4$' "$1")
{ printf '%s\n' "$l3" "$l2"; printf 'drop %s\n' "${l4#pick }"; } > "$1.new" && /bin/mv "$1.new" "$1"
EOF
chmod 755 ed-g ed-c ed-v ed-e ed-fail fakegpg seq-edit
cases.oracle: System git 2.47.3 (Debian trixie) with OpenSSH 10.0 ssh-keygen as the reference; fixture-only ed25519 keys generated in setup, no installed credentials
cases.comparison: r1: commit -S with gpg.format=ssh and a fixture ed25519 user.signingKey and fixed dates produces a commit object whose complete bytes (including the deterministic SSHSIG gpgsig header) are identical on both sides, and the signature verifies with ssh-keygen -Y verify against the fixture allowed-signers file

cases.script:
export GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_AUTHOR_NAME=Fixture GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL=fixture@example.com GIT_COMMITTER_NAME=Fixture GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL=fixture@example.com
export GIT_AUTHOR_DATE='2020-03-01T00:00:00Z' GIT_COMMITTER_DATE='2020-03-01T00:00:00Z'
K=$HOME/key
yn() { if "$@"; then echo yes; else echo no; fi; }
has() { case $1 in *"$2"*) echo yes;; *) echo no;; esac; }
cleanup() { cd /tmp/parity-case; /bin/rm -rf r; }
newrepo() { /usr/bin/git init -q -b main "$1"; cd "$1"; printf 'base\n' > f1; git add f1; git commit -q -m base; }
newrepo r
G="git -c gpg.format=ssh -c gpg.ssh.allowedSignersFile=$HOME/allowed_signers"
printf 'x\n' > f2; git add f2
git -c gpg.format=ssh -c user.signingKey="$K" commit -q -S -m good 2>/dev/null
good=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
$G verify-commit HEAD 2>"$HOME/v-good.err"; echo "good-rc=$?"
e=$(<"$HOME/v-good.err"); echo "good-reports-principal=$(has "$e" 'Good "git" signature for fixture@example.com')"
echo "good-log-show-signature=$(has "$($G log -1 --show-signature --format=%H 2>&1)" 'Good "git" signature')"
# tampered: same gpgsig header over a different message
git cat-file commit HEAD > "$HOME/c.txt"
/usr/bin/python3 -c "
d=open('$HOME/c.txt','rb').read().replace(b'\n\ngood\n',b'\n\nevil\n'); open('$HOME/t.txt','wb').write(d)"
t=$(git hash-object -t commit -w --literally "$HOME/t.txt")
$G verify-commit "$t" 2>"$HOME/v-bad.err"; echo "tampered-rejected=$(yn [ $? != 0 ])"
# unknown key
git -c gpg.format=ssh -c user.signingKey="$HOME/other" commit -q --allow-empty -S -m other 2>/dev/null
$G verify-commit HEAD 2>"$HOME/v-unk.err"; echo "unknown-key-rejected=$(yn [ $? != 0 ])"
echo "unknown-key-no-principal=$([ "$(has "$(<"$HOME/v-unk.err")" 'signature for fixture@example.com')" = no ] && echo yes || echo no)"
cleanup
